text:
The failing spec is peaking (13.98 dB vs. ≤ 2 dB), so the corrupted element should be one whose change moves peaking strongly. M4 has the largest sensitivity (+4.26 dB for +20%). Its drain is the compensation node `oa_b`, so extra width adds parasitic capacitance there and pulls the second pole down, which reduces phase margin and raises peaking. Cc is the second-strongest lever, and it's a value fault candidate. M3 and M4 are matched (same W/L and Vgs), so M4 has likely been resized rather than M3.

{"ranking": ["M4", "Cc", "M3"], "fault": "M4 (PMOS mirror load on oa_b, drain at compensation node) is oversized, adding parasitic capacitance at oa_b and lowering the second-pole phase margin, which causes the excess peaking. Its W/L no longer matches the diode-connected M3. Cc being undersized is the next candidate."}
